output.brief: Please hold the breach notice. The rise in mishandled bags looks like a tag problem, not mainly a handler problem. On 1 Sep Harlow Bay check-in switched to Fennick tag stock, the same day Tessaly took over, so the two changes coincide. Airport reader data show Corvane tags printed on Fennick stock failing automatic reading 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% on Brackwater stock in August. Corvane transfer tags and Pelion tags, which Tessaly also handles, stayed near 1.3–1.4%. On 14–16 Oct, counters briefly using Brackwater stock read at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock still failed at 12.1%. Unreadable bags go to the manual encode desk and arrive after the laterals have closed. Printer jam tickets also rose from 5 to 13 a week. Not yet established: whether the Fennick media is defective or the printers need a higher heat setting for it. Tessaly's inexperienced crews may add some problems, but the data don't show them as the main cause. Next steps: return counters and kiosks to Brackwater stock now (about five weeks are in stores and the contract is valid), then test Fennick with adjusted printer settings. Hold off on a defect claim until that test is done. Confidence is fairly high on the tag link and moderate on the rest.
